evidence_policy: Only source-explicit relationships are included in the initial corpus. Semantic normalization is permitted only when it preserves the source statement. No relationship is inferred from co-occurrence or from date ordering.

relations.name: HAS_PAYLOAD
relations.meaning: The mission or spacecraft explicitly carries or lists the payload as onboard.
relations.acceptable_evidence: A primary-source payload list, mission page, or booklet that explicitly identifies the payload as carried/onboard.

relations.name: LAUNCHED_BY
relations.meaning: The mission launch is explicitly attributed to the named launch vehicle or configuration.
relations.acceptable_evidence: An official launch archive row or mission document naming the launcher.

relations.name: LAUNCHED_ON
relations.meaning: The source-stated calendar date on which the mission launched.
relations.acceptable_evidence: An official launch archive row or mission document naming the launch date.

relations.name: LAUNCHED_FROM
relations.meaning: The site explicitly stated as the origin of the mission launch.
relations.example: AstroSat LAUNCHED_FROM Satish Dhawan Space Centre SHAR
relations.acceptable_evidence: An official launch archive statement naming the launch site.

relations.name: HAS_OBJECTIVE
relations.meaning: The source explicitly identifies the linked statement as an objective of the mission or payload.
relations.example: Chandrayaan-3 HAS_OBJECTIVE demonstrate safe and soft lunar landing
relations.acceptable_evidence: An official mission/payload objective section or statement explicitly labelled as an objective.

relations.name: DEVELOPED_BY
relations.meaning: The source explicitly credits the organization with developing the payload or spacecraft.
relations.example: Mars Colour Camera DEVELOPED_BY Space Applications Centre
relations.acceptable_evidence: A primary source using an explicit development attribution such as developed by; broad collaboration does not establish this relation.

relations.name: LED_BY
relations.meaning: The source explicitly identifies an organization or centre as leading the mission programme.
relations.example: Gaganyaan LED_BY Human Space Flight Centre
relations.acceptable_evidence: An official source explicitly calling the organization/centre the lead or stating it spearheads the programme.

relations.name: OPERATED_BY
relations.meaning: The source explicitly assigns spacecraft/mission operations to the organization or centre.
relations.acceptable_evidence: A primary source explicitly stating that the organization manages or conducts mission operations.

relations.name: OBSERVES
relations.meaning: The source explicitly states that the subject observes or measures the target/phenomenon.
relations.acceptable_evidence: A primary source explicitly describing the observation or measurement target.

relations.name: STUDIES
relations.meaning: The source explicitly states that the mission, spacecraft, or payload studies the named body, subject, or phenomenon.
relations.acceptable_evidence: A primary source explicitly using study/investigate language or an equivalent mission objective statement.

relations.name: ORBITS
relations.meaning: The source explicitly states that the spacecraft or mission is in orbit around, or placed in, the named orbit/body.
relations.acceptable_evidence: An official mission or launch source directly stating the orbit or orbiting body.

relations.name: PRECEDED_BY
relations.meaning: The source explicitly identifies the object mission as an earlier mission or predecessor in the programme sequence; chronological order alone is not sufficient.
relations.acceptable_evidence: An official source explicitly describing one mission as a follow-on to, successor of, or preceded by the other.
